headlines.text: Rewind to 2025, when Konosuke Takeshita vs. Orange Cassidy fought tooth and nail for the AEW International Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.40 ? a real highlight of the night. In a first-ever singles meeting between the two International Title mainstays, Takeshita reversed an Orange Punch attempt into a Raging Fire to retain the championship over Cassidy.

Turning the clock back to 2020: Kenny Omega vs. PAC settled things in an Iron Man (30 Minutes) match, kicking off the show on Dynamite, rated 9.14 ? a genuine showstealer in a hard-fought men's division clash. An ambitious 30-minute Iron Man match opening the entire show ? a chair shot disqualification, a shooting star press through a table, and a sudden-death overtime finish, in a match widely called one of the best AEW had produced to that point.
It was 2020 when Hikaru Shida vs. Big Swole vs. Shanna vs. Yuka Sakazaki closed out Dynamite, rated 5.92 spotlighting the women's division.

secondaries.text: Rewind to 2025, when Undisputed Kingdom (Cole, O'Reilly & Strong) vs. FTR & Garcia locked horns for the first time on Dynamite, rated 7.06 ? a solid showing.
It was 2025 when The Murder Machines kicked off their AEW journey as a team, appearing on Dynamite, rated 4.42.
On this day in 2025, Will Ospreay vs. Bryan Keith locked horns for the first time on Dynamite, rated 7.17 ? a good, competitive contest.
